newsitem.title: USA: Ohio school districts hit by GE tax refunds.
newsitem.headline: Ohio school districts hit by GE tax refunds.

text.p: Several school districts in Ohio have been hit with tax refunds for General Electric Co facilities located in the state, according to local newspaper reports.
The reports published this week indicated that the districts owe thousands of dollars in refunds of personal property taxes that were overpaid by General Electric between 1990 and 1995.
Rating agency analysts said the GE refunds would impact school districts the most because they, unlike Ohio cities and counties, rely heavily on property taxes.
The total amount of the refunds was not available from GE officials or from the Ohio Department of Taxation, which sent out refund notices to counties.

Stephanie Jarrett, tax counsel for GE Lighting, which operates 13 facilities in Ohio, said the amount of refunds is in dispute and GE has filed an appeal with the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals to resolve the amount of refunds owed.
Julie Carpenter, a spokeswoman for the state taxation department, said the amount of refunds included in the notices to the counties was confidential information that could not be released.
She said it was unclear when the refunds were to be paid by the affected governments, but an interest rate would be charged on the refund amounts.

Jarrett said GE's overpayment of taxes was uncovered by a state audit of the company's tax payments. She explained that GE had been including in its tax calculations certain parts of machinery that were actually exempt from the personal property tax.
Bill Leech, a senior analyst at Moody's Investors Service, said the agency would be contacting school districts subject to the refunds and determining the effect on their credit.

Mike Forrester, a director at Standard & Poor's Corp., said that agency was also checking into the situation and would look to see how much and when the school districts would have to pay the refunds.
In addition to its lighting operations, GE also has aircraft engine and plastics facilities in Ohio.
